t: A Tai kingdom founded in 1228 by Sukaphaa that ruled the Brahmaputra valley of Assam for six centuries.
The paik system made every free adult man owe labour or military service, supporting roads, embankments and armies.
The Ahoms resisted the Mughal Empire, winning at Saraighat in 1671, before rebellion and Burmese invasions ended the state.
dyk: Ahom kings were buried in earthen mounds called maidams at Charaideo, which UNESCO inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2024.
ev: Sukaphaa crosses the Patkai hills into the upper Brahmaputra valley
Treaty of Asurar Ali fixes a frontier with the Mughal Empire
Mir Jumla's Mughal army occupies the Ahom capital Garhgaon
Lachit Borphukan defeats the Mughals at the Battle of Saraighat
Treaty of Yandabo: Burma renounces Assam, which passes to the East India Company

f.capital: Charaideo; later Garhgaon, Rangpur and Jorhat
